summary: Sync Reserving Class with ResQ no longer refuses a Result Selection over a stray double space in a ResQ dataset name, and no longer refuses a row just because an earlier write in the same run made ResQ recalculate it.
details: ResQ names are left exactly as they are; every comparison of a ResQ name against an ArcRho name now uses the same whitespace-normalized key the review pairing already used, so each ResQ object maps onto exactly one ArcRho item.

Before each row is written only the side it is written from has to be unchanged. Saving a DFM into ResQ makes ResQ recalculate the Result Selections downstream of it, which previously failed those rows with 'Timestamp changed during synchronization'.
The change lives in the Bridge's synchronization session; the Bridge must be redeployed to pick it up.
